# OpenCode plugins Small terminal UI plugins for [OpenCode V2](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/). [![Checks](https://github.com/mxfp0/opencode-plugins/actions/workflows/checks.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mxfp0/opencode-plugins/actions/workflows/checks.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-83d996)](LICENSE) ## Plugins | Plugin | What it does | | --- | --- | | [Skill status](plugins/skill-status) | Shows loaded skills in a collapsible sidebar section, even at low verbosity. | ## Install Requires OpenCode V2. Tested with **2.0.31**. Clone this repository: ```sh git clone https://github.com/mxfp0/opencode-plugins.git ``` Add the plugin folder's absolute path to the `plugins` array in `~/.config/opencode/cli.json`. Keep any existing entries: ```json { "plugins": [ "/absolute/path/to/opencode-plugins/plugins/skill-status" ] } ``` Restart OpenCode. The **Skills** section appears in the right sidebar. Click its heading to collapse or expand it. OpenCode supplies the runtime dependencies. No build or dependency installation is needed to use the plugin. To update, run `git pull` in the cloned repository and restart OpenCode. ## Develop Use [Bun](https://bun.sh/) 1.3.14: ```sh bun install bun run typecheck bun run test ``` Each plugin lives in `plugins//` with its own package manifest and README. See [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) to add one. ## License [MIT](LICENSE)

# Skill status A collapsible **Skills** section in the OpenCode V2 sidebar. Green dots mark loaded skills. The list stays visible at low transcript verbosity. ## Install Follow the [repository installation instructions](../../README.md#install), using this folder as the plugin path in `cli.json`. ## Behavior - Shows skills selected with a prompt, explicitly activated skills, and successful `skill` tool calls. - Lists each skill once, alphabetically, using its ID. - Restores the list when you reopen a session. - Keeps skills through context compaction and message-cache refreshes. - Removes skills that appeared only in messages deleted by a committed revert. - Wraps long names and follows the current theme. The list covers the whole session, not just the current turn. It records which skills were loaded; it does not indicate whether their instructions remain in the model's current context. Click **Skills** to collapse or expand the list. An empty session shows `None loaded`. If history cannot be read, the section shows `History unavailable` alongside any known skills. The section uses the standard sidebar, so it is hidden when the sidebar is hidden. Subagent sessions have their own lists. ## Development Run the checks from the repository root: ```sh bun run typecheck bun run test ``` Tests use the real Solid runtime and OpenTUI test renderer. They cover live updates, failed calls, duplicate loads, history pagination, cache refreshes, reverts, session switching, creation races, text wrapping, and cleanup.

# Contributing

Keep each plugin independent in `plugins/<name>/`.

A CLI plugin needs:

- A `package.json` that exports `./tui`.
- A TUI entrypoint using the [OpenCode V2 plugin API](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/cli).
- A README with install instructions and any version requirements.
- Tests for its observable behavior.

Register development dependencies at the repository root. OpenCode supplies runtime packages such as `@opencode/plugin/tui`, `@opentui/core`, and `solid-js`.

Before opening a pull request:

```sh
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run typecheck
bun run test
```

For UI changes, also load the plugin in OpenCode and check its appearance and interactions. Add new plugins to the table in the root README.
